page.layout: One text column, with the running head and page number at the top. Below the last line, a short parenthetical "(Deus.)" set right of centre.

main_text.p: se habere putauerunt. Impleta est terra e-ius argento & auro, nec est finis thesauris eius: sed & equis repleta est terra eius, & non est finis quadrigis eius. Repleta quoq; est terra eius diis uanis: & coram opere manuum suarum se incuruauerunt, atq; coram eo quod fecerunt digiti eius. Et inclinatus est homo, & humiliatus est vir: tu verò (Domine) non remittes eis. Ingredere in petrā, & abscondere in puluere, à facie pauoris divini, & propter gloriam magnificetię eius. Sublimitas oculorum hominis humiliabitur, & incuruabitur altitudo hominum: atque exaltabitur Dominus solus in die illa. Quoniā dies Domini exercituū (erit) super omne superbū & excelsum, atq; super omnem eleuatū, ut humilietur. Etiā super omnes cedros Libani sublimes & eleuatas, & super omnes quercus Basan. Deniq; super oēs mōtes excelsos, & super cunctos colles eleuatos. Et super omne turrim excelsam, & super omne murū munitū. Super uniuersas quoq; naues Tharsis, & super oēs desiderabiles figuras. Et incuruabitur celsitudo hominis, atq; humiliabitur altitudo hominū: & exaltabitur solus Dominus in die illa. Idola autē in uniuersum exterminabit

page.notes: The page has no marginal notes. "(Deus.)" is set in the text block, right of centre, below the last line; I have kept it as its own paragraph. Doubtful readings: "omne" in "super omne superbū" may carry an accent; "magnificetię" may have a tilde over the e; "oēs" and "mōtes" are read from abbreviation marks that are faint. Long s is printed as f-like in several places and is transcribed as s. "dijs" was changed to "diis" under the i/j rule.
